fields.old: Crushing Impact. Weapon-branch only (when: !isSpell && effDef > atk, today's exact gate). fields.new: Crushing Impact. Weapon-branch only (when: !isSpell && effDef > atk, today's exact gate). Value delegates to crushingImpactMultiplier(holder, role) -- Amendment 1 gap close (19 Nov): reads ctx.holder/ctx.role, not ctx.state, so a future widening of `holders` resolves correctly for whichever holder actually wears the gear; for today's player-only holders this is ctx.state under a different name, byte-identical. Thraekor:6/Vanguard:4/Ashforged:6's own upgrades are now registered entries (Rule 1, tag effect:crushing_impact, below) instead of an inline Math.max -- M1 no longer warns about them.

fields.old: Executioner. Value delegates to executionerMultiplier(state) unchanged, which itself reads executionerThreshold(state) (Drake Hunter:4/Vanguard:6/Contract Hunter:4's own upgrades, already folded in there) -- those three set tiers still owe M1 a registry entry of their own, deferred.
fields.new: Executioner. Amendment 1 gap close (19 Nov): unifies the player-only executionerMultiplier(state) (combat.js) and the already-generalized-but-separate executionerMultiplierFor(attacker, defenderHp, defenderMaxHp) (the same file -- used by the ally/enemy attack-roll formulas in actions.js, flat 30% threshold, no set-widening) into ONE entry, dispatched by calculateOutgoingMultiplier for every attacker role. `holders` widens to ally/enemy here specifically (not R1 -- this is correcting the entry to match what the code already did via that second function, not a new behavior) because executionerMultiplierFor already granted this to any attacker wearing the effect; executionerThreshold(holder, role)'s own upgrade entries (Drake Hunter:4/Vanguard:6/Contract Hunter:4) stay holders: ['player'], so an ally/enemy attacker still gets exactly the old flat 30% -- byte-identical in both directions. ctx.defenderHp/defenderMaxHp are populated generically by every call site (today: activeEnemySlot(combat) for the player, the explicit hp/maxHp or health/maxHealth args the old executionerMultiplierFor took, for ally/enemy).
